title: Could Erling Haaland survive as a gladiator in ancient Rome?
caption: Could Erling Haaland survive as a gladiator in ancient Rome? We asked the Colosseum. And a lion. ⚔️🦁 #could #haaland #gladiator #ancientrome #football #history #whatif #fyp

scenes.text: Could Erling Haaland survive as a gladiator in ancient Rome? {{ev}}We looked at the evidence. {{sci}}Scientifically. ||0.2|| {{long}}From a safe distance.

In the red corner: {{name}}Erling Haaland. {{h}}{1.94|One point nine four} metres of Norwegian striker. {{sp}}Top speed: around thirty six kilometres per hour. {{goals}}Thirty six Premier League goals in one season. {{diet}}He famously eats cow heart and liver. ||0.3|| {{zen}}Then he meditates.

In the blue corner: {{name}}the Colosseum. {{cap}}Around fifty thousand spectators. {{opp}}Opponents with swords, nets and tridents. {{barley}}Gladiators were nicknamed barley men. ||0.3|| {{veg}}They were mostly vegetarian.

Round one. {{t}}The murmillo. {{arm}}Sword, big helmet, and a shield the size of a door. {{shot}}Haaland does what he does best. {{kick}}He shoots. ||0.3|| {{hit}}The shield does not survive. {{goal}}Neither does the murmillo's confidence.

Round two. {{t}}The retiarius. {{net}}He fights with a trident and a net. {{throw}}He throws the net. ||0.3|| {{home}}Haaland has spent his entire career in the back of the net. {{feel}}He feels right at home.

Round three. {{t}}The lion. {{v}}A lion sprints at up to eighty kilometres per hour. {{h}}Haaland: thirty six. {{run}}Running away is not an option. ||0.4|| {{zen}}So he sits down and meditates. {{lion}}The lion, confused, sits down next to him.

The verdict. {{q}}Could Erling Haaland survive as a gladiator? ||0.5|| {{yes}}Yes. ||0.4|| {{hist}}Historically, around nine in ten gladiator fights ended without a death. {{crowd}}And fifty thousand Romans would chant his name. {{p1}}Chance of survival: high. {{p2}}Chance he meditates in the middle of the Colosseum: ||0.25|| {{p3}}one hundred percent.
